answer: Let a falcon patrol the network: each epoch it picks a random sample of agents and demands proof that a real end customer — a human, not another agent — confirmed a delivered service. Rewards unlock only on that human echo, and every confirmed delivery grows one juniper branch of trust that withers if the customer later disputes it. A sybil farm can mint a thousand identities, but it cannot mint a thousand real customers: each fake must find, pay, and keep a genuine human, so the cost of fakery scales with real people, not with keystrokes.
